title: Introduction
description: Choose the local tools gateway or the existing Discord agent engine.
text:
Your agent.
A little more reach. Plompy Local connects an agent on your computer to selected tools running behind a local MCP endpoint. Your host client, such as Codex, Claude Code or OpenCode, plans the task and writes the response. Plompy handles the enabled integrations and local artifacts. Plompy Local is a source-build preview on the repository's main branch. Build it with compose.local.yaml . It is separate from the published 0.12.0 Discord engine image, which does not contain this mode. Check Compatibility and verification (compatibility.md) for what has actually been tested. Pick your starting point - Run locally with Docker (quickstart.md): start the tools gateway, connect a client, and try a small task. - Research companies and draft messages (research.md): gather public evidence and save drafts without connecting a mailbox. - Use the existing Discord engine (discord.md): let Plompy run a coding agent from your private Discord threads. Two ways to use Plompy Plompy Local Discord engine --- --- --- Conversation Your own MCP client A private Discord thread Agent Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode or another compatible client The runner selected by the engine Plompy provides Selected tools and artifact storage Queue, runner sessions, memory and recovery Model credentials in the container Not required Required by the selected runner Discord configuration Not required Required Compose file compose.local.yaml compose.yaml The local gateway does not start a second model behind your host agent. It does not give Plompy access to every account or tool on your computer. What stays with you Configuration, gateway credentials and generated files live in separate Docker volumes. You choose which integrations to enable. External search services and your model provider may receive task data when you use them. Read Permissions and data flow (security.md) before connecting accounts. No Plompy subscription or account is needed. Model access and third-party integrations may have their own charges.

title: Run locally with Docker
description: Build the local gateway and connect your chosen host MCP client.
text:
Run locally with Docker

Build the Local MCP preview from the repository's  main  branch. These commands build from source; they do not pull a published Plompy Local image. Do not use the  v0.12.0  release tag for this quickstart.

   Before you start

Install Git and Docker with Compose. Choose a host MCP client such as Codex, Claude Code or OpenCode, with its usual model access configured. The Plompy container does not need model credentials or a Discord token. See  Requirements (requirements.md).

Clone the source into a new directory, then build the core gateway:

 

   Initialize the private volumes

 

Initialization creates a private configuration and local access token. It preserves existing configuration. Secrets are stored separately from artifacts.

   Start the gateway

 

The default endpoint is  http://127.0.0.1:7331/mcp . Docker publishes it on host loopback only. The process listens on the container interface so the published port is reachable. A normal browser visit is not a connection test: the endpoint requires MCP and a bearer token.

   Check the local protocol

 

This initializes MCP and calls local status. It deliberately avoids remote tool discovery and does not contact vendors or a model.

   Connect your agent

The gateway is client-neutral. Choose the configuration for your installed client:

-  Codex (codex.md): Streamable HTTP with a bearer-token environment reference.
-  Claude Code (claude-code.md): HTTP MCP with an environment-based authorization header.
-  OpenCode (opencode.md): explicit V1 or V2 configuration.
-  Other MCP clients (other-clients.md): connection requirements and compatibility limits.

For local inference, see  Ollama with your agent (ollama.md). Ollama provides the model; your agent remains the MCP client.

Keep the local token in a private environment, separate from the project. Each client guide shows its configuration format. Model login stays in your client; Plompy does not import it.

   Check the client connection

Use your client's MCP connection check before starting a model task. Then ask it:

 

A configured entry, a connected server and a completed tool call are separate checks. A model-powered tool call may consume your client model allowance.

   Add one search integration

For a company-research task, enable one search provider.  Firecrawl (integrations/firecrawl.md) supports a limited keyless path and a separately configured API-key path.  Perplexity (integrations/perplexity.md) requires your own API access. Review their costs before running an external test.

Add the  browser profile (browser.md) only if the pages you need require a rendered browser. Basic public page fetching is available in the core profile.

   Try a bounded task

 

Inspect the sources and drafts yourself. Expand to 30 companies once the small task produces useful evidence. See  the complete research example (research.md).

title: How it works
description: Understand the client, gateway, integration and artifact boundaries.
text:
One conversation. Selected tools.

The local mode follows a single agent loop:

 

   Your client decides what to do

The host client owns the conversation, model selection, planning and tool choice. Its own permissions still apply. Adding Plompy does not remove your client's existing tools or isolate its shell.

   Plompy exposes a small tool surface

The gateway validates requests, authenticates the client, exposes only selected tools and enforces bounded calls. It does not offer a generic shell, browser script executor or arbitrary integration invocation tool.

The standard MCP SDK handles initialization, discovery and calls over Streamable HTTP at  /mcp . The gateway has no Discord connection and does not load the engine's runner authentication.

   Integrations remain separate

The existing catalog identifies supported services. Local mode adds an explicit research policy on top: a configured service and an allowed tool name are both required. A missing or failing integration is reported separately; it does not make unrelated local tools unavailable.

API-key services reuse the fixed vendor definitions and private credential handling from Plompy's existing MCP bridge. GitHub uses a dedicated read adapter for  gh . It is not treated as an existing MCP server.

   Files survive container replacement

Configuration, secrets and artifacts use separate named volumes. A rebuilt image does not remove them. Do not run Compose with volume deletion unless you intend to erase that data. See  Backups and updates (maintenance.md).

   Where code lives

- Engine and canonical Markdown:  dalkedev/plompy-engine (https://github.com/dalkedev/plompy-engine).
- Local gateway:  packages/local-mcp/ .
- CLI:  scripts/local-integrations.mjs , reached through the existing integrations command.
- Local containers:  Dockerfile.local  and  compose.local.yaml .
- Website: the existing static Plompy site, built from HTML, CSS and JavaScript. Documentation pages are generated from the engine's  docs/local/  Markdown.

A copy of documentation in a browser is not a connection to a local gateway. The website never requests your integration keys or automatically contacts localhost.

title: Installation and requirements
description: Check the host, container, model and integration requirements.
text:
What you need

   On your computer

- Docker Engine or Docker Desktop with Docker Compose.
- Git and a source checkout containing  compose.local.yaml .
- A compatible host MCP client, such as Codex, Claude Code or OpenCode, configured with a model you can use.
- A free host port,  7331  by default.

Docker runs the gateway on Linux. macOS and Windows users need Docker's Linux container environment. Platform-specific acceptance results belong in  Compatibility (compatibility.md); do not assume every platform has been tested because the image can build.

   Inside the image

The local image uses the repository's pinned Node 26 runtime and committed dependency lock. The core target contains the gateway and its light dependencies. The optional browser target adds the pinned Playwright/Chromium dependencies.

The process runs without root privileges. There is no Docker socket mount, full home-directory mount, privileged container or automatic import of host accounts.

   Model and integration access

Keep model credentials in your host client. Plompy Local needs no model subscription or agent account of its own. See  client connection options (other-clients.md).

Each external integration has separate requirements. A model subscription is not automatically a Perplexity API allowance or a Firecrawl subscription. Read the  integration catalog (integrations.md) before enabling a provider.

   Source builds only for this extension

The existing  ghcr.io/dalkedev/plompy-engine:0.12.0  image belongs to the Discord/Codex engine. It is not a Plompy Local image. Build the local Dockerfile from the repository's  main  branch. No Plompy Local registry image is published for this preview.

   Running without Docker

The package can also run with Node 26.13.0 or a newer Node 26 release, the committed lock, and a private configuration outside the checkout. This is useful for development. Docker is the documented onboarding path; host mode has the permissions of the host user.

Do not reuse a private Discord engine workspace as the local gateway's artifact or credential directory.

title: Choose your client
description: Connect a host agent supporting Streamable HTTP and private bearer authentication.
text:
Choose your MCP client

Plompy Local is a tools server. You choose the agent and model on your host. It does not depend on OpenCode's agent loop.

   Documented clients

  Client   Connection guide   Configuration form  
  ---   ---   ---  
  Codex    Connect Codex (codex.md)   TOML server entry with bearer-token environment variable  
  Claude Code    Connect Claude Code (claude-code.md)   HTTP MCP server with environment-based authorization header  
  OpenCode    Connect OpenCode (opencode.md)   Explicit V1 or V2 remote MCP JSON  

The generator commands contain no real token. They do not copy model logins, provider keys or other host credentials into Docker.

   Local model option

 Ollama (ollama.md) can provide local inference to a compatible host agent. It is a model provider, not another MCP client. Tool access still goes through the agent and the Plompy gateway.

   Requirements for another client

A compatible client must support MCP Streamable HTTP, the endpoint  http://127.0.0.1:7331/mcp , and an  Authorization: Bearer  header supplied through its private credential mechanism. It must support MCP initialization, discovery and tool calls.

Keep the token outside checked-in project configuration. If a client only accepts literal secrets in a shared file or cannot attach an authorization header, do not weaken gateway authentication to make it connect.

   Localhost means the client's machine

The default endpoint is reachable from the host running Docker. A cloud-hosted agent cannot reach your laptop's loopback. A client running in a separate container also has a different loopback interface. This first setup does not provide a public tunnel or a remote-access deployment.

Do not publish port 7331 to the internet as a shortcut. Choose a deliberately secured remote architecture separately if you need one.

   Test one layer at a time

First run the  gateway protocol check (quickstart.md check-the-local-protocol). Then verify the client's connection and ask it to call  plompy_status . Finally enable and test one integration with a small task.

An MCP-compatible label is not evidence that every client version has been tested. Read  Compatibility and verification (compatibility.md) for the exact clients and acceptance limits.

   Provide the token privately

In a private terminal with shell tracing disabled:

 

Use  local-browser  if that is the running service. The variable must exist in the process that launches Codex. A separately launched desktop app does not automatically inherit this terminal environment. Do not paste the token into project files or screenshots. Read  Credentials (credentials.md) for storage and cleanup.

   Verify the connection

Use  codex mcp list  to inspect registration. Then start a Codex session and ask it to call  plompy_status . Registration alone does not prove a completed MCP call or a working model account.

Codex's own permissions and tools remain in effect. Adding the Plompy research profile does not restrict Codex's separate shell, browser or other integrations. See  verification results (compatibility.md) for the tested boundary.

   Recorded client check

On 12 November 2026, the actual Codex  0.159.2  CLI parsed the generated configuration and completed  plompy_status  against Docker. The test used an isolated client directory and a deterministic local Responses mock, which received two model requests. It asserted a completed MCP tool event. This verifies the client-to-tool path, not a paid model account or research reasoning quality.

title: Connecting Claude Code
description: Connect Claude Code over HTTP without sharing model credentials with Docker.
text:
Connect Claude Code

Run the  Docker quickstart (quickstart.md) first. Claude Code keeps its own model login on your host. Plompy adds selected tools through an HTTP MCP connection.

   Generate a configuration fragment

 

The output is:

 

Claude Code expands the environment variable in the header. Preserve the literal  ${PLOMPY_LOCAL_TOKEN}  reference when saving JSON; do not expand it into a real token in a shell-generated file. Merge the entry with your existing MCP configuration rather than overwriting it. The generator is print-only.

   Register with the CLI

The installed Claude Code CLI  2.1.197  supports HTTP MCP. Use single quotes around the header so your shell preserves the variable reference:

 

Choose the configuration scope appropriate to your project. Inspect an existing  plompy  entry before replacing it. The  official Claude Code MCP guide (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp) explains scopes, environment expansion and client-side permission prompts.

   Provide the token privately

In a private terminal with shell tracing disabled:

 

Use  local-browser  if that is the running service. Keep the environment available to the Claude process, then unset it or close the terminal when finished. See  Credentials (credentials.md). A GUI client started elsewhere may not inherit this environment.

   Verify before research

Use  claude mcp list  to inspect server connectivity. In an interactive Claude Code session,  /mcp  shows connected servers and tools. Ask Claude to call  plompy_status  before requesting research.

A server connection check does not prove model access, an integration's API key or a completed research result. Claude Code's separate tools and permission settings are unchanged. See  verification results (compatibility.md).

   Recorded client check

On 12 November 2026, Claude Code  2.1.197  reported Connected after an authenticated MCP health check against the Docker gateway. The test used isolated home/configuration and a private token environment. No Claude agent or model turn was run, so this check does not establish model-powered tool execution.

title: Connecting OpenCode
description: Use the correct V1 or V2 schema and keep the local token out of project files.
text:
Connect OpenCode

Plompy Local is a remote MCP server from the client's point of view, even when its HTTP endpoint is on your own laptop.

   Select the correct schema

 

OpenCode V1 places entries directly under  mcp  and uses  enabled . V2 places them under  mcp.servers  and uses  disabled . Do not combine these schemas. The existing Discord runner is independently pinned to OpenCode  1.19.5 ; that does not upgrade your host client.

Generate the matching fragment:

 

   V1 example

 

   V2 example

 

These examples contain no real token. Give  PLOMPY_LOCAL_TOKEN  to the OpenCode process through a private shell session or secret manager. Never paste the token into a repository, URL, issue, screenshot or shared transcript. See  Credentials (credentials.md) for the private container-to-host handoff.

   Hand the token to your host client

In a private host terminal, with shell tracing disabled, capture the token into
the environment without printing it:

 

Use  local-browser  instead of  local  if that is the running service. Do not run
this with  set -x  or copy the resulting environment into diagnostics. Close the
session or  unset PLOMPY_LOCAL_TOKEN  when finished. The command contains no secret
literal; the value remains a secret in the host process environment. Other code
running with the same host account may be able to inspect that environment.

   Preserve your existing configuration

Merge the fragment into your current OpenCode configuration. Preserve other servers, providers and permission rules. The generator prints a fragment by default. An explicit file update must show the change, preserve unrelated fields and create a backup. JSONC comments require a JSONC-aware edit; do not overwrite a commented file with a plain JSON parser.

   Verify in two steps

First, use  opencode mcp list . Then ask OpenCode to call  plompy_status . The list checks discovery; the tool call checks that the agent can use the connection.

A model-powered call may consume your model allowance. The offline acceptance harness uses synthetic input and does not prove that a paid provider account is working.

   Instructions are separate

The  agent instructions (research.md agent-instructions) explain how to use sources and save results. They do not establish MCP connectivity. Conversely, adding MCP does not automatically install those instructions in your project.

See the  official OpenCode MCP documentation (https://opencode.ai/docs/mcp-servers/) for the current client and version-specific migration guidance.

   Recorded client check

On 12 November 2026, the actual OpenCode  1.19.5  client completed eight MCP calls against Docker in an isolated synthetic research run. It read a fixture search page and three browser-rendered sources, produced two deduplicated company records, exported JSON and CSV, and read the CSV back. The model was a deterministic local fixture, not paid live inference. OpenCode V2 was not run in this acceptance check.

title: Local models with Ollama
description: Use Ollama as the host agent model provider while Plompy supplies MCP tools.
text:
Keep your model local with Ollama

Ollama is a model provider, not an MCP client. Run a compatible agent such as Codex, Claude Code or OpenCode on your host, connect it to Ollama for inference, and connect that same agent to Plompy for tools.

 

The Plompy container does not need a model or an Ollama login. This path has not been run in the current acceptance checks; no Ollama model was downloaded. See  Compatibility (compatibility.md).

   Choose a tool-capable model

Use an installed model that supports tool calls and your chosen client. A model that chats successfully may still fail to select a tool, produce valid arguments or follow source requirements. The client integrations recommend a large context window, commonly at least 64k tokens. Larger contexts and models require more memory; choose them for your machine.

Follow the current  Ollama integration guides (https://docs.ollama.com/integrations/overview) for model compatibility and setup. Review any model download's size and license yourself before installing it.

   OpenCode with Ollama

After installing and configuring Ollama, its integration launcher can configure OpenCode:

 

Then add the Plompy MCP entry from  Connecting OpenCode (opencode.md), matching your installed V1 or V2 version. Preserve the model-provider configuration created by the launcher. Do not paste an older V1 provider block into V2 without checking its schema.

The  official OpenCode integration guide (https://docs.ollama.com/integrations/opencode) also describes manual provider configuration. Its local OpenAI-compatible endpoint is typically  http://localhost:11434/v1 .

   Codex with Ollama

Replace  YOUR_INSTALLED_MODEL  with the exact name of an installed tool-capable model before running this template:

 

Set up the  Codex MCP connection (codex.md) separately and provide  PLOMPY_LOCAL_TOKEN  to the same Codex process.  --oss  changes the model-provider path; it does not configure Plompy for you. See  Ollama's Codex guide (https://docs.ollama.com/integrations/codex).

   Claude Code with Ollama

Ollama provides a Claude Code launcher:

 

Its documented manual environment route is below. Replace  YOUR_INSTALLED_MODEL  before running; the quoted name is a placeholder, not a recommended model:

 

These values select Ollama's local compatibility endpoint;  ollama  here is the documented placeholder, not a real vendor credential. Keep your  Claude Code MCP connection (claude-code.md) and local Plompy token configured separately. Follow  Ollama's Claude Code guide (https://docs.ollama.com/integrations/claude-code) for current client compatibility.

   Local inference and external requests

Local inference keeps the selected model call on your machine when the model and endpoint are local. Research tools still fetch public sites. Enabled Firecrawl, Perplexity, PostHog and other remote integrations can receive requests and task data. Ollama also offers cloud models, so check the actual selected model and endpoint before assuming inference is local.

Start with a small status and page-read task. Inspect the tool calls and source URLs before asking a model to produce a larger company list. Plompy's no-send research profile remains the same regardless of which model you choose.

title: Integration catalog
description: Choose integrations deliberately and understand their actual local-mode status.
text:
Connect only what you need

The default research profile exposes basic public page reads and local artifacts. Add one search service if you need discovery; add the browser profile if pages need rendering.

A configured key is not proof that an account works. Status distinguishes configuration from tool discovery and actual successful calls. Live tests that contact an external service are opt-in and may consume its allowance.

   Local-mode matrix

  Integration   Local-mode role   Authentication   Container requirement   Limit  
  ---   ---   ---   ---   ---  
   Public web (integrations/web.md)   Read public HTTP(S) pages   None   Core image   No private network or authenticated browser session  
   Playwright (integrations/playwright.md)   Render a page and extract text/links   None   Browser profile   Read-only, sandbox enabled  
   GitHub (integrations/github.md)   Selected repository reads   Dedicated GitHub token required   Core  gh  adapter   No arbitrary commands or writes  
   Firecrawl (integrations/firecrawl.md)   Search and scraping   Keyless limits or own API key   Core plus network   Explicit tool allowlist  
   Perplexity (integrations/perplexity.md)   Search and research   Own API key   Core plus network   API billing separate from consumer subscription  
   OpenAI Docs (integrations/openai-docs.md)   Official documentation   Public endpoint   Core plus network   Documentation, not company search  
   Context7 (integrations/context7.md)   Library documentation   Endpoint-dependent   Core plus network   Vendor rate limits  
   PostHog (integrations/posthog.md)   Product analytics reads   Scoped personal API key   Core plus network   Existing project access required  
   Custom MCP (integrations/custom.md)   Existing runner integration   Runner-specific   Not exposed by local research profile   Tool names and annotations cannot prove read-only behavior  
   TinyFish (integrations/tinyfish.md)   Existing runner integration   Runner-native auth   Not exposed by local research profile   Autonomous actions need a separate policy  
   Camoufox (integrations/camoufox.md)   Existing host browser integration   Host setup   Not supported in local Docker profile   Use Playwright for this local flow  

   Configuration versus availability

-   Registered:   the integration exists in the catalog.
-   Configured:   local settings are present.
-   Needs authentication:   credentials are missing or rejected.
-   Available:   the adapter can expose the selected tools.
-   Live-tested:   a real external call succeeded in the reported test scope.
-   Unsupported:   this profile cannot run the integration.

The exact status response contains the available evidence. Do not convert “configured” into “live-tested” in reports or UI.

   Explicit tools

Remote tool names are selected by the operator and intersected with the research policy. A provider adding new tools does not silently grant them to the agent. The gateway does not expose an unrestricted  execute  or  invoke  escape hatch.

   Changing integrations

Use the same integrations CLI with  --mode local . The existing  --runner  paths remain for the Discord engine. Restart the gateway after changing its configuration so discovery reflects the new selection.

An explicit remote discovery diagnostic initializes MCP and lists permitted tools; it does not call a search or scrape tool:

 

The  --live  flag permits contacting that configured service. A subsequent authorized tool call is required before claiming the task or integration is live-tested.

title: Credentials and OAuth
description: Keep local access and vendor credentials separate from project and artifact data.
text:
Credentials belong outside the project

There are two kinds of secrets: the local bearer token used by your host client to reach Plompy, and optional integration credentials used by Plompy to reach a vendor. They are separate and are never interchangeable.

   Private storage

The initialization command creates configuration and a gateway token in separate named Docker volumes. Secret directories use owner-only permissions and files use  0600 . The gateway validates credential files before use and rejects unsafe links or ownership.

Artifacts are stored in a third volume. Do not copy credentials into generated CSV, JSON, reports, agent instructions or Git.

   Provide the token to the host client

Your host client needs the local token in its own process environment as  PLOMPY_LOCAL_TOKEN , or through a supported private file reference. Use the private container-to-host handoff below. Do not display it in a shared terminal or save it in the project configuration.

The generated client configurations include an environment reference, not a literal secret. Environment references work only if that environment variable exists when the host client starts. A variable inside the Plompy container is not automatically available to your host client process.

   Hand the token to your host client

In a private host terminal, with shell tracing disabled, capture the token into
the environment without printing it:

 

Use  local-browser  instead of  local  if that is the running service. Do not run
this with  set -x  or copy the resulting environment into diagnostics. Close the
session or  unset PLOMPY_LOCAL_TOKEN  when finished. The command contains no secret
literal; the value remains a secret in the host process environment. Other code
running with the same host account may be able to inspect that environment.

   Add a vendor key

Use the CLI's credential input through stdin. It must not be passed as a command-line argument. Command history, process listings and copied diagnostics can expose arguments.

For example, after configuring Firecrawl API-key mode, run this in a private Bash or Zsh terminal with tracing disabled. Enter the key when  read  waits; it will not echo.

 

Use the intended integration ID and running service. Existing credentials are preserved unless you explicitly request  --replace .

A key's presence is a configuration check. Use an explicitly requested live test to verify that the provider accepts it. That test may have a cost or consume the provider's quota.

   OAuth boundaries

The new local gateway does not implement vendor OAuth storage or browser login. Use its supported API-key or keyless paths. Existing host runners can use their native remote MCP OAuth flow as documented in the  existing integrations guide (https://github.com/dalkedev/plompy-engine/blob/main/docs/integrations.md).

A host runner's OAuth session is not imported into Docker. Enabling a service in local mode does not silently start login or copy a browser profile.

   Remove or rotate

Remove an integration's configuration with the local CLI, restart the gateway, and delete or rotate that integration's dedicated credential using the private credential workflow. Revocation at the provider is a separate step. Do not delete unrelated credentials or the entire secret volume to remove one integration.

Rotating the gateway token requires updating the host client's private environment and reconnecting your client. Keep backups of secret volumes encrypted and outside your repository.

title: Browser setup
description: Use the optional container browser with sandboxed, read-only navigation.
text:
Bring a browser when a page needs one

Start with the public web tool. Enable Playwright for pages whose useful content appears only after JavaScript renders. The local browser tool reads a page; it does not expose a complete browser automation session.

   Enable the optional profile

Stop the core service before using the browser service: both publish the same loopback port and use the same private volumes.

 

Run local status and ask your host client to rediscover tools. A core image with a Playwright entry in its config does not acquire Chromium automatically; it must use the browser image.

   What the tool returns

 browser_read  returns bounded page text, title, links and explicitly published email addresses with their source URL and timestamp. Pages are treated as untrusted input. A published email address has not been verified for deliverability.

   Browser boundaries

- Fresh contexts do not import host cookies or sessions.
- Chromium sandboxing stays enabled.
- Navigation and subresource requests pass through the public-network policy.
- The profile exposes no arbitrary JavaScript execution, form submission, file upload or generic click tool.
- Private network destinations, metadata endpoints and unsafe redirects are blocked by default.

This deliberately narrower browser surface fits research and evidence collection. The existing host Playwright integration offers different capabilities and should not be confused with this profile.

   Bounded page rendering

A browser read has a 30-second operation limit, a 60-request ceiling, at most four concurrent resource fetches, a 5 MiB transfer budget and a 100,000-character text limit. Images, media, fonts, WebSockets, service workers, popups and subsequent frame navigations are not supported. A page depending on those features may be incomplete.

The container uses the dedicated  scripts/docker-browser-seccomp.json  profile for the browser sandbox. It does not enable privileged mode or mount syscalls.

   If the sandbox cannot start

Read the actual container diagnostic and platform compatibility results. Do not add  --no-sandbox ,  privileged , a Docker socket or a full home mount as a quick fix. The repository's smoke test must show the browser launch and page read on the target environment before you claim browser support there.

 Camoufox (integrations/camoufox.md) is not bundled or advertised as working in this new local container. Its existing Linux host setup remains separate.

title: Permissions and security
description: Understand access checks, data flow and the limits of a local container.
text:
Keep the boundary visible

The research profile reads public sources and writes local artifacts. It does not send email, publish posts, buy anything, delete remote data or modify repositories.

   Local connection

The Compose port is bound to  127.0.0.1 . The gateway requires a bearer token, validates Host and checks browser Origin headers. No browser origin is allowed by default. The website does not call this endpoint.

Do not expose the port through a tunnel or change the host binding to  0.0.0.0  as part of this quickstart. A remote deployment needs a separate threat model, TLS and access design.

   Tool permissions

Enabled integrations and explicit tool names define the gateway's surface. Model-generated text saying “the user approved” cannot change it. The profile has no generic shell or invoke tool for bypassing those decisions.

Your host client's own tools are separate. Adding Plompy does not sandbox its shell, disable its other MCP servers or prevent its model from using existing capabilities. Review the client's permissions for your task.

   Public web is untrusted

A webpage may contain text asking an agent to reveal secrets or ignore instructions. Treat that content as evidence to analyze, never as authority. Do not follow instructions embedded in company sites or tool results.

URL fetching rejects private, loopback and link-local destinations, including metadata endpoints. Redirects are checked again. Browser subresources follow the same public-network boundary. Local fixture exceptions exist only for controlled tests.

   Where data can travel

  Data   Possible destination  
  ---   ---  
  Task text and selected tool results   Your selected model provider, local or hosted  
  Search query   Your chosen search service  
  Requested URL   Website host and, for hosted scraping, the integration provider  
  Extracted public content   Gateway, host client and its selected model provider  
  Exported results   Local artifact volume; later wherever you copy them  
  Vendor credential   Its configured authentication destination  

Docker does not make every part of this workflow offline. It also does not protect against all same-user host access, a compromised runtime, or a malicious external provider.

   Bounded failure

Calls have concurrency, time and response-size limits. A failed service is reported separately from other integrations. The gateway does not automatically retry uncertain external operations. Inspect outcomes before repeating a task that may consume credits.

   Evidence, not guarantees

Store the exact source of an email address and distinguish “published on this page” from deliverability verification. Review drafts before using them. This version intentionally does not connect a mailbox or implement bulk sending.

title: Files and exports
description: Save bounded CSV, JSON and Markdown artifacts without overwriting unrelated files.
text:
Results you can inspect

The local artifact tools store files in the dedicated artifact volume. Use JSON for structured evidence, CSV for a spreadsheet, and Markdown for a readable summary or drafts.

   Export a result

Ask your host agent to use  artifacts_export  with a descriptive basename and the matching format. CSV and JSON accept structured records. Markdown accepts text content.

 

   File rules

Names are flat basenames inside the configured artifact directory. Traversal paths and symlink targets are rejected. The tool does not overwrite an unrelated file. Repeating an identical export can return the existing result; changing the content requires a new name.

Exports are bounded. Split a large result into explicit batches instead of asking the model to bypass limits. The response includes a file name, size and content hash so you can identify the output.

   CSV handling

CSV values that could be interpreted as spreadsheet formulas are escaped. This protects exported text such as a company name beginning with  = . Normal CSV quoting alone does not provide that protection.

Keep source URLs and evidence status in the export. Do not include credentials, session cookies or private account contents.

   List and read

Use  artifacts_list  to discover saved files and  artifacts_read  to inspect a file. Readback checks that the intended result exists; a tool's queue receipt is not a completed file export.

   Retrieve files on the host

The files remain in a Docker volume until you copy them out. From your host, create a new private directory and copy only the artifact directory:

 

Use  local-browser  if that is the running service. Choose a new destination instead of overwriting an existing result directory. Do not mount your entire home directory to make retrieval easier.

For backups and cleanup, see  Updates, backup and uninstall (maintenance.md).

title: Company research and drafts
description: Find public company evidence and prepare university-project messages without sending.
text:
Find a project partner. Keep the evidence.

This example uses the general tools to research companies and draft messages. It does not turn Plompy into a mailing platform and needs no mailbox credentials.

   Describe the project first

Give your agent facts it can use: the degree or course, the kind of application you can build, the project deadline, your skills, preferred location, and whether the work is a prototype or production deliverable. Do not let it invent your experience, a partnership or promises you cannot keep.

   Start with a small batch

Connect a  search provider (integrations.md), basic page reading and artifact storage. Use  Playwright (browser.md) only when needed. Verify a few results before increasing the batch.

 

For the larger run, replace 3 with 30. The requested count is a ceiling, not permission to fill gaps with made-up data.

   Export fields

  Field   Meaning  
  ---   ---  
   company_name    Name shown by the source  
   website    Official website  
   industry    Source-supported description  
   location    Published location or empty  
   public_email    Explicitly published business contact or empty  
   source_url    Exact page that supports the contact  
   checked_at    Time the page was checked  
   match_reason    Factual explanation of relevance  
   evidence_status    For example  published_on_official_site , not  deliverability_verified   
   draft_subject    Proposed subject line  
   draft_body    Draft only  

Use additional evidence URLs if a match reason and email are supported by different pages. A directory's claim about a company is not equivalent to confirmation on the company's website.

   Review the result

Open the cited pages. Check the proposed match, email source, spelling and the claims about you. Remove unrelated contacts. Edit each draft in your own voice before deciding how to contact a company.

No test or example in this repository sends mail. Actual sending is outside this first profile.

   Agent instructions

The source checkout includes  examples/local/AGENTS.md  and  examples/local/company-research.md . Merge the instructions deliberately into the project used by your host client: use its supported instruction file, such as  AGENTS.md  for Codex/OpenCode or  CLAUDE.md  for Claude Code. Preserve existing project guidance and fill in your own project context. They explain source handling and draft-only behavior; they do not configure MCP.

title: Updates, backup and uninstall
description: Replace the image while preserving private configuration, secrets and results.
text:
Keep your data when you update

The local image and the private volumes have different lifecycles. Rebuilding or replacing a container should not erase your integrations and results.

   Update from source

Review and obtain the intended source revision. Stop the service, rebuild the chosen target and start it again. Do not run a destructive Git reset in a checkout containing your work.

 

For the browser variant, use  --profile browser  and  local-browser . Keep the previous source revision available until the updated service passes its connection and artifact checks.

   Back up three things

- Configuration volume: enabled integrations and server settings.
- Secret volume: local token and integration keys, stored in an encrypted private backup.
- Artifact volume: generated files and their provenance.

Stop writes before taking a consistent volume backup. Record the source revision and image used. Do not commit private volume exports to the repository. Test restoration in a separate Compose project before depending on a backup.

   Remove one integration

Use the local CLI's remove command, then restart the gateway. This removes only the selected configuration. Provider-side key revocation is separate. Keep unrelated integrations and artifact files.

   Stop without deleting

 

This removes the local containers and network but preserves named volumes. It does not remove the existing Discord engine's separate deployment.

   Uninstall deliberately

Disconnect the  plompy  entry from the host client and remove its local token reference. Back up wanted files, revoke vendor credentials you no longer need, and remove only this deployment's volumes when you intend to erase them.

 docker compose down --volumes  deletes persisted data. It is not a routine update or troubleshooting step.

title: Existing Discord mode
description: Keep the original runner engine and the new local tools gateway separate.
text:
Discord mode is still here

The original engine accepts tasks from private Discord threads, stores work in a durable queue and launches a coding runner. That deployment uses  compose.yaml , its private environment file, its runner credentials and its own volumes.

The new local gateway uses  compose.local.yaml  and does not require a Discord token or channel. It does not start, migrate or restart your existing Discord bot.

   Existing documentation

-  Docker engine setup (https://github.com/dalkedev/plompy-engine/blob/main/docs/docker.md)
-  Runner support and boundaries (https://github.com/dalkedev/plompy-engine/blob/main/docs/runners.md)
-  Runner integrations (https://github.com/dalkedev/plompy-engine/blob/main/docs/integrations.md)
-  Configuration (https://github.com/dalkedev/plompy-engine/blob/main/docs/configuration.md)
-  State backups (https://github.com/dalkedev/plompy-engine/blob/main/docs/state-backups.md)

   Different OpenCode roles

In Discord mode, the engine's experimental OpenCode adapter starts the pinned runner to execute a job. In local mode, your independently running OpenCode client calls Plompy's tools.

Do not point the host client at an engine-managed private runner directory. Do not copy Discord memory, bot credentials or runner auth into the local artifact volume.

   No automatic migration

There is no need to rename the existing environment, move its state or replace its Compose file to try local tools. Enable the new mode alongside it using separate private volumes and the documented loopback port.

title: Compatibility and verification
description: Separate implementation, offline checks, container evidence and external-account tests.
text:
What has been verified

These pages describe the Local MCP source-build preview on the repository's  main  branch. Publishing its documentation does not create a container release. Local mode is not included in  v0.12.0 , and no Plompy Local registry image is published for this preview.

   Version boundaries

  Component   Contract  
  ---   ---  
  Local runtime   Node 26.13.0 or newer Node 26  
  MCP SDK   Pinned by  packages/local-mcp/package-lock.json   
  Docker   Source build from  Dockerfile.local   
  Host clients   Codex and Claude Code export; explicit OpenCode V1 or V2 config  
  Local inference   Ollama configuration guide, not tested in this acceptance run  
  Existing engine OpenCode runner   Independently pinned to 1.19.5  
  Browser   Pinned optional Playwright dependency, sandbox enabled  
  Existing published engine release   0.12.0, Discord/Codex image  

   Verification levels

-   Offline:   synthetic credentials, local fixtures and controlled responses. This can verify validation and error handling without proving vendor access.
-   Container:   the actual built image starts, authenticates an MCP client and performs the checked local operations.
-   Real browser:   Chromium runs inside the browser image and reads a controlled fixture with sandboxing enabled.
-   Real OpenCode client:   the actual client discovers or calls the gateway. A deterministic model fixture is not a real model-provider acceptance test.
-   Live provider:   an explicitly authorized call to a real account succeeds. Record provider, tool, date and outcome without secrets.

   Acceptance record

The following checks were completed on 12 November 2026. The test sources and reproducible commands are in the  local MCP test guide (https://github.com/dalkedev/plompy-engine/blob/main/packages/local-mcp/test/README.md).

  Check   Result and boundary  
  ---   ---  
  Core and browser Docker images   Both source targets built successfully. No image was pushed to a registry.  
  Real sandboxed browser   Chromium ran as UID 1000 with no sandbox-disabling flag. It read JavaScript-rendered contacts, retained the final source URL, and blocked POST and metadata requests.  
  Actual Codex 0.159.2 client   An isolated client parsed the generated TOML and completed  plompy_status  against Docker. A deterministic local Responses mock handled two model requests; a completed MCP tool event was asserted.  
  Actual Claude Code 2.1.197 client   An isolated client completed an authenticated MCP connection health check and reported Connected. No Claude agent/model turn was run.  
  Actual OpenCode 1.19.5 client   An isolated client completed eight real MCP calls against Docker for a synthetic research task. A deterministic local mock model directed the calls.  
  Research artifacts   Three controlled source pages produced two deduplicated company records, draft content, JSON and CSV. Stored files and formula-safe CSV were checked.  
  Container restart   Configuration, gateway token and exact artifact bytes persisted across a real restart.  
  Public OpenAI Docs   Real remote initialization and  search_openai_docs  with query  API Responses  and limit 1 succeeded at 15:31 UTC. No model account or paid inference was used.  
  Other paid API providers   Not live-tested with account credentials. Offline validation does not prove provider access.  
  OpenCode V2   Configuration generation is supported; the V2 client was not exercised in the recorded acceptance run.  
  Ollama   Documented setup only. Ollama and local-model quality were not tested, and no model was downloaded.  

A configuration export or CLI registration alone must not be described as a completed model-powered task. The Codex and OpenCode checks used actual clients with controlled model fixtures; the Claude Code check covered authenticated server connectivity only.

The synthetic research test proves client transport, tool execution, rendering and persistence. It does not prove live search-provider coverage, paid model reasoning quality, mailbox access or email deliverability. Third-party integration failures remain possible because of authentication, plan limits, changed tool names or service availability.

   Deliberate first-version limits

- No email sending, mailbox integration or bulk outreach.
- No nested agent or model inside the gateway.
- No automatic import of host credentials or browser profiles.
- No vendor OAuth implementation in the gateway.
- No Camoufox Docker support in this profile.
- No TinyFish autonomous task tool in the research profile.
- No arbitrary custom MCP servers in the local research profile.
- No generic shell, arbitrary browser script or unrestricted tool-invocation endpoint.
- Documentation content is English; the existing landing retains English and Polish routes.

title: Troubleshooting
description: Diagnose the exact failing layer instead of assuming that a process means success.
text:
Find the failing layer

Check container startup, MCP authentication, tool discovery and actual tool execution separately. A running PID or a successful browser request is not proof of the whole flow.

   Connection refused

Check  docker compose -f compose.local.yaml ps  and confirm the selected service is running. Core and browser services share port  7331 ; do not start both at once. Confirm that the container listener is reachable through the loopback publication.

The host client URL is  http://127.0.0.1:7331/mcp . Inside a different container,  127.0.0.1  means that other container. This quickstart places the MCP client on the host.

   Unauthorized or forbidden

Verify that the host client process has the correct token reference and that it was restarted after an environment change. Do not paste tokens into logs while diagnosing it. Check the configured Host/Origin values if you deliberately changed the endpoint. A normal webpage is not an approved MCP client.

   Unknown configuration field

Check  opencode --version . V1 uses  mcp  entries and  enabled ; V2 uses  mcp.servers  and  disabled . Regenerate the fragment for the installed client. Do not upgrade the engine's separately pinned runner while fixing a host-client configuration.

   Connected, but the tool is missing

Inspect local status. An integration must be enabled, supported by the image, authenticated when required and allowed by its tool policy. Restart the gateway after config changes and reconnect the client. A newly added vendor tool is not automatically permitted.

   Key exists, but the provider rejects it

Key presence only proves local configuration. Check the provider account, API product, scope and billing status yourself, then run one explicit live test. A consumer subscription may not include API access. Never repeatedly retry uncertain paid calls.

   Rate limit or timeout

Read the integration-specific error. Reduce batch size and wait according to the provider's guidance. Other integrations should remain usable. Do not describe incomplete results as a successful 30-company export.

   Browser unavailable

Use the browser image and profile, not just the core image with a Playwright configuration entry. Verify the sandbox diagnostic for the host platform. Do not disable sandboxing to silence the error.

   URL denied

Private network addresses, local endpoints, metadata services and unsafe redirects are blocked. A publicly named domain resolving to a private address is still private. Test-only fixture exceptions are not a general intranet feature.

   Export rejected

Use a flat basename with the correct extension. Choose a new filename if a different artifact already exists. Keep rows and content within tool limits. Inspect the result with  artifacts_read  and verify the reported hash.

   Where to report a problem

Include the source revision, operating system, Docker and host client versions, the step that failed and a redacted error. Exclude tokens, private config files, cookies, company drafts and account data unless you deliberately intend to share them.

title: Public web
description: Read public webpages without a vendor account.
text:
Read the public web

The built-in  web_fetch  tool retrieves public HTTP(S) pages with bounded response sizes. It is enabled in the default local configuration and needs no external API key.

   Set up

 

Restart the service after configuration changes. Use local status to check whether the integration is enabled.

   Try it

 

   What it costs

There is no Plompy API fee. Requests go directly to the website. Your host model and network still have their own costs.

   Limits

This is page reading, not a search index or an authenticated browsing session. Use a configured search provider for discovery and Playwright when rendering is necessary. Private addresses, unsafe redirects, credential-bearing URLs and oversized responses are rejected.

   Connection test

The ordinary local  test  initializes MCP and calls local status without fetching a public page or listing remote tools. To verify web access, deliberately ask the agent to read one public URL you have selected. Report that exact URL and result, not general internet compatibility.

title: Playwright
description: Render public pages in the optional sandboxed browser image.
text:
Playwright

The local  browser_read  tool renders public pages in a fresh Chromium context and returns bounded text, links and published contacts. It is a narrow read adapter, not the full runner-facing Playwright MCP catalog.

   Set up

Follow  Browser setup (../browser.md) to build and start  local-browser . The pinned dependency comes from the existing  packages/playwright  lock. Setting an integration flag in the core image does not install a browser.

   Authentication and cost

No vendor API key is needed. The browser does not import your logged-in profiles or cookies. Rendering consumes local CPU and memory; public websites and your host model still receive the data described in  Security (../security.md).

   Try it

 

   Boundaries

Chromium sandboxing stays enabled. Requests are checked against the public-network policy. There are no generic clicking, form, upload or script-evaluation tools. Sites needing a login, CAPTCHA or unsupported interactions may remain unreadable.

   Connection test

Run the container browser smoke test from the implementation's verification instructions. It must launch a real browser and read a controlled fixture. A successful host browser test alone is not evidence for Docker support. See  Compatibility (../compatibility.md).

title: GitHub
description: Use a controlled read adapter instead of unrestricted GitHub CLI commands.
text:
GitHub

Plompy's existing GitHub integration uses  gh . The local gateway wraps selected read operations rather than pretending that  gh  is a remote MCP server.

   Set up

 

The current adapter requires a dedicated, minimally scoped GitHub token even when reading public repositories. Provide it through the local credential command or an explicitly configured private file. Do not import the host's complete GitHub config or use your primary token merely because it is convenient.

   Permissions

This research profile does not expose arbitrary  gh  arguments, shell commands, repository writes, issue creation, comments, pull requests or merges. The two tools are  github_search_repositories  (a query, at most 20 results) and  github_repository  (an owner and repository name). Inspect their schemas in the client before using the adapter.

   Try it

 

   Costs and diagnostics

GitHub account, API and rate limits apply. Credential presence is not proof of access to a repository. A live test must target a deliberately selected repository and report the result; never open an issue or write a comment as a smoke test.

GitHub is optional for company research. Public company websites can be read without it.

title: Firecrawl
description: Add hosted search and page extraction with explicit read tools.
text:
Firecrawl

Firecrawl can discover pages and extract their content. It is an external service: queries and requested URLs leave your computer. The gateway supports an explicitly selected tool subset.

   Limited keyless setup

 

Keyless access is subject to the vendor's current restrictions and availability. It is not a promise of an unlimited free plan.

   API-key setup

Choose API-key mode and provide a dedicated key through the private credential workflow. Do not type the key in the command arguments or save it in your client project configuration. The local gateway does not perform Firecrawl OAuth login.

   Try it

 

   Read-only argument surface

The gateway limits  firecrawl_search  to a query and bounded result count.  firecrawl_scrape  accepts a public URL, optional main-content extraction and only Markdown, HTML or links as output formats.  firecrawl_map  accepts a URL, optional search text and a bounded result count. Browser actions, arbitrary JavaScript and extra upstream arguments are rejected.

   Costs and limits

Your account, credits, rate limits and the vendor's terms apply. Search and scraping can consume credits. No extra provider calls are made merely by reading local configuration status.

Discovery and a real tool call are different checks. Run an explicit live diagnostic, then one small search you approve. Never treat a stored key as proof of a successful search.

The gateway exposes only configured read tools that pass its research policy. It does not automatically enable new crawl, agent or mutation tools when the vendor adds them.

See  Firecrawl MCP documentation (https://docs.firecrawl.dev/mcp-server) for provider requirements.

title: Perplexity
description: Use your own API access for source-oriented search.
text:
Perplexity

The Perplexity integration provides hosted search and research tools. Local mode uses a dedicated API key and the fixed vendor MCP endpoint. The existing runner-native OAuth path remains separate.

   Set up

 

Add the key through the private credential command. Restart the gateway and reconnect the client. Missing credentials should produce an authentication-required status for this integration, without breaking other tools.

   Try it

 

   Costs

Perplexity API usage belongs to your API organization and allowance. A consumer subscription does not establish API access. Search or research calls may be billed. Start with a small query and check the provider's current pricing.

   Evidence and limitations

Search output helps discover candidates; it does not replace reading the cited company source. Keep the exact contact page for an email address. Report rate limits, authentication failures and incomplete batches honestly.

A live tool test is opt-in. No real Perplexity account success is implied by the offline tests. See  provider MCP documentation (https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/getting-started/integrations/mcp-server).

title: OpenAI Docs
description: Read official developer documentation through its public MCP endpoint.
text:
OpenAI Docs

This integration connects to the public official developer-documentation MCP server. It is useful for implementation questions and API documentation, not finding companies or email contacts.

   Set up

 

The catalog uses  https://developers.openai.com/mcp . No model account is installed in Plompy by this action. Only the explicitly selected documentation tools are exposed.

   Try it

 

   Authentication, cost and limits

This documentation endpoint does not use your model API key. Availability and rate limits remain the provider's responsibility. Your host model may still incur usage when it processes the results.

Run an explicit discovery check and a small documentation query to verify the current endpoint and selected tool names. Do not label the integration live-tested solely because its public URL is configured.

   Verification evidence

On 12 November 2026 at 15:31 UTC, the implementation check initialized the real public endpoint and completed  search_openai_docs  with query  API Responses  and limit 1. This used no model account or paid inference. A successful check on that date does not guarantee future service availability.

title: Context7
description: Resolve a library and query its documentation.
text:
Context7

Context7 supplies library documentation to an agent. It is a hosted documentation service, not a general company-search integration.

   Set up

 

The configured public HTTPS endpoint is  https://mcp.context7.com/mcp . Use only authentication modes actually supported by the local adapter. A provider's native client OAuth flow is not automatically supported by the gateway.

   Try it

 

   Costs and diagnostics

Provider limits and account requirements may change. Configure a supported credential only if your chosen service access requires it. Run a deliberate live test to establish current access; configuration alone proves no entitlement or reachability.

The selected tool names are checked during discovery. If a vendor changes its catalog, inspect and review the new names instead of adding a wildcard.

title: PostHog
description: Read an existing project with a scoped credential and read-only restrictions.
text:
PostHog

PostHog can help an agent inspect an existing product's analytics. It does not add analytics or tracking to the Plompy website and is not needed for company discovery.

   Set up

For project discovery, enable the fixed read tool explicitly:

 

Other permitted names are  event-definitions-list ,  insights-get-all ,  insight-get ,  dashboards-get-all  and  dashboard-get , when the upstream actually advertises them. Select only the tools needed for your task. Provide a scoped personal API key through the credential workflow. Do not expose an entire account's catalog automatically.

The gateway reuses the fixed PostHog destination and read-only request header from the managed bridge. Its local tool allowlist remains a separate restriction.

   Try it

 

   Authentication and costs

You need access to the intended PostHog project. Existing query costs and account limits may apply. The local gateway does not import a runner's OAuth login.

   Test deliberately

A configured credential is not proof of the intended project access. Run an explicit read-only live test against that project. Never create an event, dashboard, annotation or other remote object merely to verify connectivity.

Do not put personal analytics data into company-research exports. Read  data flow (../security.md) before allowing a model to process private project results.

title: Custom MCP
description: Understand why arbitrary custom tools are excluded from the first research profile.
text:
Custom MCP

Custom MCP remains available in the existing runner integration system. It is not exposed by the first local research profile.

   Why this profile does not enable it

An arbitrary server can give a sending or mutation tool a harmless name and a read-only annotation. An allowlist of names alone would not establish the research profile's promise that it cannot send messages or change external state.

The local CLI therefore rejects enabling custom MCP. Local status identifies it as unsupported, while the existing Discord runner configuration remains unchanged.

   Existing runner setup

Follow the  runner integrations guide (https://github.com/dalkedev/plompy-engine/blob/main/docs/integrations.md) for operator-reviewed remote or stdio servers. Those tools run under that runner's permissions and are not part of the local research contract.

Authentication, dependencies, account access and costs depend on the chosen server. A new integration needs an adapter with explicit semantics, documented permissions and meaningful tests before it joins this profile.

   Alternative for the local workflow

Use the implemented public web and browser readers plus the fixed, selected search integrations in the  catalog (../integrations.md). Do not route a forbidden action through a generic custom tool.

No custom gateway connectivity or live acceptance is claimed.

title: Camoufox
description: Understand the existing host integration and its local-container limitation.
text:
Camoufox

Camoufox remains available through Plompy's existing Linux host integration. It needs its separately provisioned Python environment, browser and private display.

   Local Docker status

Camoufox is not supported in the new local research container. This documentation does not present it as a tested Docker feature. Use the  Playwright browser profile (../browser.md) for the container workflow.

   Existing host setup

Follow the  existing browser and integrations documentation (https://github.com/dalkedev/plompy-engine/blob/main/docs/integrations.md). That setup is distinct from connecting a host MCP client to Plompy Local.

Do not copy private cookies or profile directories from a running Discord deployment into the new gateway. A host configuration or package import passing does not demonstrate an operational browser in Docker.

   Authentication and costs

The host browser uses the operator's deliberately provisioned session and permissions. Websites and any services used have their own access conditions. The local gateway does not start an authorization flow or charge a Camoufox fee.

   Testing

The existing Python offline suite checks its code paths. A real browser test must be performed separately in the actual supported host environment. No local Docker Camoufox acceptance is claimed.

title: TinyFish
description: Keep autonomous remote browser actions outside the first research profile.
text:
TinyFish

TinyFish is present in the existing integration catalog and can be configured for engine-managed runners. Its remote agent tools can perform actions, so they are not automatically treated as read-only company-research tools.

   Local profile status

The first local research profile does not expose TinyFish autonomous task execution. A service being registered in the shared catalog does not mean every operation is allowed in this mode.

Use  public page reading (web.md),  Playwright (playwright.md) and an explicitly selected  search provider (../integrations.md) for the documented company workflow.

   Existing runner path

The  runner integration guide (https://github.com/dalkedev/plompy-engine/blob/main/docs/integrations.md) describes TinyFish configuration and authentication. Native runner OAuth and API-key bridge settings remain separate from this gateway.

   Costs and uncertainty

Remote agent runs may consume credits and can have effects on websites. Do not automatically repeat an uncertain run. Check the vendor's result before deciding to retry. Never use a real form submission or message as a connectivity test.

Adding a future local adapter requires an actual policy boundary and appropriate acceptance tests; a read-only label in documentation would not provide that boundary.
